claim: The added comment asserts a universal: '$3 is non-empty ONLY on the `implement` arm. Every other class's <candidate_number> is a PR number' and that devflow.yml's trigger negating /prflow:implement makes class `implement` reachable only from devflow-implement.yml.
source_excerpt:
# $3 is non-empty ONLY on the `implement` arm. Every other class's <candidate_number> is
# a PR number, so emitting it here would key the PR-less record to a PR as if it were an
# issue. devflow.yml's trigger negates /prflow:implement, so class `implement` reaches
# this glue only from devflow-implement.yml, whose candidate is the issue number.
verify_against: .github/workflows/devflow.yml trigger `if:` conditions and its command-class resolver
verify_hint: Attempt to falsify: construct a devflow.yml-dispatched comment/command that normalizes to class `implement` (e.g. an alias spelling such as /devflow:implement, or a resolver path devflow.yml allows) and check whether it reaches prepare-harness-floor.sh with a PR number as <candidate_number>

claim: The added comment in _resolve_pr_for_issue asserts that an assignment made inside the function would 'always read empty' in the parent because the sole caller uses command substitution — a universal about the caller set.
source_excerpt:
Reports WHICH failure fired through its EXIT CODE, never a variable: the sole caller
# invokes this in a command substitution, so an assignment made here happens in a
# subshell the parent never sees, and the reason would always read empty.
verify_against: All call sites of _resolve_pr_for_issue in scripts/prepare-harness-floor.sh and any test driver
verify_hint: Grep `_resolve_pr_for_issue` across the repo (including lib/test/modules/) and confirm there is exactly one caller and it is a command substitution
